$comment:
The shared part-content-encoding case table. One rule across eight accepted OAS
editions, both form media types, six declared part kinds, four Content-vocabulary
spellings and two Encoding Object contentType settings: contentEncoding and
contentMediaType have force only where the resolved part schema declares
`type: string`. On a declared non-string type they are inert and the part keeps
its own per-type default row; a part declaring no `type` is the separate
type-absent cell and is unchanged by either keyword.

EVERY harness that executes this file renders the case as a WHOLE OpenAPI
document and loads it through its own engine's shipped loader — the two Go
engines, openapi-client/typescript, and openbindings-ts/packages/openapi against
the BUILT client dist. No harness hands the engine a hand-built typed model.

The rendered decision deliberately carries no part headers other than
Content-Type. A multipart part's Content-Transfer-Encoding is emitted by the Go
engines and cannot be emitted by the TypeScript one, which writes parts through
FormData; that difference predates this table and is pinned in each Go engine's
own tests rather than smuggled across the twin boundary here. A bare FormData
string field carries no Content-Type header at all, which [RFC7578] Section 4.4
makes the same wire fact as an explicit text/plain, so both spellings render as
`text/plain:<body>`.
UPDATED 2026-08-17: the 80 urlencoded cells on 3.0.0, 3.0.1, 3.0.2 and 3.0.3
moved, and none of the `bases` did. Until then a legacyOpenAPIFormEncoding
predicate in all three engines put those four editions' control-free urlencoded
parts on the RFC6570-style path, where the Encoding Object was never consulted
at all: an object rode as its own exploded members, an array as repeated
parameters, and a declared `encoding.contentType: text/plain` on either was
silently DISCARDED. On the content path the declaration is honoured, so an
object or array under an explicit text/plain now refuses before dispatch —
openbindings.openapi@1 §9.2's "a member for which the resolved schema leaves no
faithful form carriage refuses before dispatch". The predicate was deleted
because each of those editions' own §4.1 tells tooling to make no distinction
between the patch versions of the 3.0 line, and 3.0.4 — a 3.0.* version —
states that with all three RFC6570-style fields absent "Encoding is to be based
on contentType alone" (ruling:
design/openapi-30-urlencoded-default-lane-ruling.md; specification:
openbindings.openapi@1 §2 and §9.2). The `bases` are keyed by edition LINE and
describe the part-default row rather than the path, which is why they are
unchanged: this table's own rule never depended on the patch component.

bases.3.0|array-of-string|contentEncoding|encC: 3.0 line: neither Content-vocabulary keyword is in the Wright-Draft-00 Schema Object, so it is inert and the array-of-string part decides exactly as its |plain twin.
